title: INT8 activation harmonizer pipeline and hotpatch kernel adapters
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Implement an activation-aware INT8 calibration and runtime integration that harmonizes cross-layer activation scales (SmoothQuant-style) and ships lightweight kernel adapters that allow hotpatch fallback on older microkernels. The work includes a calibration pipeline, per-workload profile storage, CI evaluation harness for accuracy/regression detection, and runtime shims to select adapted kernels when a harmonized quant profile is active.
background: Customers running large decoder-only models saw accuracy regressions when deploying naive per-weight INT8 quantization on KV-cache heavy workloads. SmoothQuant-style activation scaling reduces outlier activations and recovers accuracy, but requires coordination between calibration profiles and runtime execution (kernel ordering, fused ops, prefetched KV). Past tickets implemented static calibration and separate runtime patches, but we need an integrated, low-latency solution that supports hotpatching kernel adapters without full model reloads and that scales to our Dedicated and Private runtimes.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a calibration pipeline that computes per-layer activation scale factors and stores them as a compact "harmonizer" profile tied to model-version and sequence-length buckets. 2) Extend the quant-profile registry to expose compatibility metadata so the router can select harmonized profiles by policy. 3) Implement runtime kernel adapters: small shims that translate INT8 kernel inputs/outputs with activation rescale steps so existing microkernels can run with harmony profiles. 4) Add a hotpatch mechanism to apply kernel adapters at runtime for active model endpoints with zero downtime fallback to the original kernel. 5) Add CI jobs to run standardized eval prompt sets and measure accuracy/latency/regressions across profiles.
tasks: Calibration pipeline: data collection harness and per-layer scale estimator
Profile storage: add harmonizer profile format to model registry
Compatibility metadata: runtime selection rules and policy config
Kernel adapters: implement rescale pre/post-shims for core matmul and attention kernels
Hotpatch system: safe swap-in and swap-out of kernel adapters at runtime
CI/bench: accuracy regression tests and latency microbench for NVidia A100 and T4
Documentation: migration guide and console UI fields for profile selection
milestones: M1: Calibration pipeline prototype + profile format (2025-02-28)
M2: Kernel adapter prototype and unit tests (2025-03-07)
M3: Hotpatch integration + end-to-end smoke tests on staging (2025-03-14)
M4: CI accuracy/regression harness and dashboard panels (2025-03-18)
acceptance_criteria: Harmonizer profile can be generated from the calibration pipeline and uploaded to the registry
Runtime can apply kernel adapters via hotpatch without restarting the model worker
Accuracy regression against baseline FP16 <= 1.0% average MRR on standard eval set for Llama-2-13B-like family
p50 token latency increase <= 8% and p99 <= 20% vs unharmonized INT8 baseline on target hardware
Automated CI evaluates profile and flags regressions before merge
testing_plan: Unit tests for scale estimator and profile serialization
Integration test: calibration -> registry -> runtime selection -> inference output equivalence checks
Hardware benchmarks on A100/T4 with KV-prefetch scenarios and varying seq-len
A/B rollout in staging: 10% traffic with harmonized profile, monitor perplexity/MRR and latency
Chaos test: simulate kernel adapter failure and verify graceful fallback to original kernel
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dev branch prototype and design review
Stage 1: Staging release with synthetic load and eval suite
Stage 2: Canary on non-critical tenants with monitoring and kill-switch
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 100% for models that meet accuracy/latency gates
Stage 4: Offer harmonized profiles in Dedicated console UI as opt-in
risks_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected accuracy regressions on niche inputs -> Mitigation: conservative default profile and holdback list for known-sensitive models
Risk: Hotpatch instability -> Mitigation: time-limited canaries and automatic rollback on error metrics
Risk: Kernel adapter overhead increases latency -> Mitigation: micro-optimizations in shims and selective adapter use only for layers identified by cost-benefit analysis
Risk: Profile storage inconsistency across regions -> Mitigation: canonical registry replication and version pinning in deployment configs
